description: Na₂Be(GeO₃)₂ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Fdd2 space group. There are four inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.25-2.70 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.44-2.86 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.28-2.84 Å. In the fourth Na site, Na is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with two equivalent BeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with six GeO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one BeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.27-2.42 Å. There are two inequivalent Be sites. In the first Be site, Be is bonded to four O atoms to form BeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four GeO₄ tetrahedra and corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are a spread of Be-O bond distances ranging from 1.63-1.67 Å. In the second Be site, Be is bonded to four O atoms to form BeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four GeO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are two shorter (1.64 Å) and two longer (1.65 Å) Be-O bond lengths. There are four inequivalent Ge sites. In the first Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent BeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra, and corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are two shorter (1.72 Å) and two longer (1.78 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. In the second Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent BeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra, and corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are two shorter (1.73 Å) and two longer (1.79 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. In the third Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two BeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two GeO₄ tetrahedra, and corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.72-1.79 Å. In the fourth Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two BeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two GeO₄ tetrahedra, and corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.73-1.80 Å. There are nine inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na and two Ge atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two Na and two Ge atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Be, and one Ge atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Be, and one Ge atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two Na, one Be, and one Ge atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two Na, one Be, and one Ge atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two Na, one Be, and one Ge atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded to two Na and two Ge atoms to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₂Ge₂ tetrahedra. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Be, and one Ge atom.
